name: Fetal Lower Urinary Tract Obstruction
aliases: Lower Urinary Tract Obstruction in Fetus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnostic Criteria for LUTO

criteria.description: Presence of an abnormally enlarged fetal bladder (megacystis) on prenatal ultrasound
Oligohydramnios or anhydramnios indicating reduced amniotic fluid volume
Bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with dilated ureters and renal pelvis
Thickened bladder wall on ultrasound imaging
Male fetal sex confirmed by ultrasound or genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of megacystis and oligohydramnios on prenatal ultrasound with or without supporting findings such as dilated ureters or thickened bladder wall.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on prenatal ultrasound findings; fetal MRI may be used as adjunctive imaging.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged fetal bladder detected on ultrasound
Reduced amniotic fluid volume secondary to impaired fetal urine output

common.notes: Dilation of ureters and renal pelvis due to urinary obstruction
Secondary to oligohydramnios affecting lung development
Abnormal kidney development due to obstruction

occasional.notes: Fetal fluid accumulation in the abdomen
Urine leakage causing fluid collection around the kidney
Severe fetal edema due to heart failure or anemia

searchTerms: fluid in abdomen from urine leak
urine in abdominal cavity with inflammation

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic urinary tract obstruction
Rare spontaneous rupture of the fetal bladder

laboratory: Amniotic fluid analysis may show low volume and altered electrolyte composition
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing megacystis, oligohydramnios, hydroureteronephrosis
Fetal MRI for detailed urinary tract and lung assessment
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromes such as Prune Belly syndrome
other: Fetal urine sampling may be performed for assessment of renal function

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or deficient abdominal wall musculature
Characteristic triad differentiates from isolated LUTO
Valve leaflets causing obstruction in posterior urethra
Confirmed by fetal cystoscopy or postnatal imaging
Most common cause of LUTO in male fetuses

redFlags: Severe oligohydramnios leading to pulmonary hypoplasia
Progressive renal dysplasia with impaired fetal renal function
Fetal hydrops indicating cardiac failure or severe compromise
references: Nicolaides KH, et al. Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction: diagnosis and management. Prenat Diagn. 2019.
Orphanet: Fetal lower urinary tract obstruction. ORPHA:435365.
Kirkpatrick AW, et al. Prenatal diagnosis and management of fetal lower urinary tract obstruction. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol. 2020.
